title: Which change data capture tool fits you?

questions.hint: A free licence still has a bill: servers and people on call.

options.label: A vendor runs it for me
options.why: you want a vendor to run it, and you run OLake Go yourself

options.label: My team runs it on our own servers
My cloud's own service (AWS or Google)
options.why: you want your cloud's own service, and you run OLake Go yourself

questions.q: Where does the data need to land?

options.label: Apache Iceberg tables in my own storage
options.why: you want Iceberg tables you control

options.label: A warehouse such as BigQuery
options.why: you want a warehouse writer, and OLake Go writes Iceberg and Parquet (warehouses can query those tables, per our compatibility page)

options.label: Kafka topics, for many consumers
options.why: you want a stream into Kafka, and OLake Go writes Iceberg and Parquet

options.label: Postgres, MySQL, MongoDB or SQL Server
options.why: the tools in the post's table list these four databases

options.label: Oracle at large scale, or a mainframe
options.why: you need Oracle or mainframe capture, and OLake Go's change capture covers PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB and SQL Server

options.label: Databases plus many SaaS apps
options.why: you need SaaS apps too, and OLake Go's sources are databases, Kafka and S3

questions.q: How fresh does the data need to be?

options.label: As close to continuous as I can get
options.why: you want a continuous stream, not scheduled syncs: Debezium and Flink CDC stream events, and Estuary describes real-time or batch delivery (a vendor claim)

options.label: Kafka
options.why: Debezium can run inside Kafka Connect

options.label: Flink
options.why: Flink CDC fits teams that already run Flink

options.label: Neither, and I would rather not add them
options.why: you do not want to run a streaming stack just for this (Debezium Server runs without Kafka)

debezium.name: Debezium
debezium.summary: An open-source, log-based CDC tool that runs inside Kafka Connect, or as Debezium Server.
debezium.bestWhen: you already run Kafka and want one stream feeding many consumers.
debezium.watchOut: you run all of it, and the Apache Iceberg sink lives in a separate community repository.

flink.name: Flink CDC
flink.summary: Write a YAML pipeline and it generates and submits the Flink job for you.
flink.bestWhen: Flink is already in your stack and you want transforms.
flink.watchOut: you need a Flink cluster, and the Iceberg sink needs a primary key on every table and is at least once.

olake.name: OLake Go
olake.summary: Open-source, log-based CDC that copies PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB and SQL Server changes into Apache Iceberg or Parquet on your own storage.
olake.bestWhen: you run PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB or SQL Server and want Iceberg tables you control.
olake.watchOut: it runs on your own infrastructure and writes Iceberg and Parquet.

fivetran.name: Fivetran
fivetran.summary: A vendor-run service with hundreds of connectors, billed on Monthly Active Rows per connection.
fivetran.bestWhen: you want someone else to run it and can budget for usage-based pricing.
fivetran.watchOut: the bill counts changed rows per connection, and the Iceberg service does not support position deletes.

estuary.name: Estuary or Artie
estuary.summary: Vendor-run capture with usage pricing. Estuary mixes streaming and batch, and Artie publishes a monthly plan.
estuary.bestWhen: you want a managed platform and a price you can see.
estuary.watchOut: Estuary's Iceberg route needs S3 and Spark, and Artie lists Iceberg and Oracle only under Enterprise.

airbyte.name: Airbyte
airbyte.summary: Scheduled syncs, 700+ connectors, a free Core edition and an Iceberg destination.
airbyte.bestWhen: a delay of minutes to an hour is fine and you want lots of connectors.
airbyte.watchOut: syncs are scheduled, not a live stream, and Core uses the Elastic License 2.0, a source-available licence rather than Apache 2.0.

enterprise.name: Striim, Qlik Replicate or GoldenGate
enterprise.summary: Enterprise platforms with documented Oracle log readers. Qlik Replicate also lists mainframe sources.
enterprise.bestWhen: Oracle is your main source and you are fine talking to sales.
enterprise.watchOut: Striim and Qlik publish no prices and GoldenGate is priced per processor or user, and their Iceberg support has limits: Striim's Iceberg Writer supports only Google Cloud Storage (it documents a separate S3 Tables writer), and Qlik's comes mainly from a separate feature.

cloud.name: AWS DMS or Datastream
cloud.summary: Cloud-native services for teams that live on one cloud.
cloud.bestWhen: you are on AWS or Google Cloud and want migration or replication on one cloud.
cloud.watchOut: AWS's DMS target list does not include Iceberg and its CDC page says there is no latency guarantee, and Datastream's Iceberg output is append-only.
